complianceRequirements: Compliance with 40 CFR 63, MACT Subpart ZZZZ and 40 CFR 60, NSPS Subpart IIII.
Maintain documentation of control devices installation.
Install, maintain, calibrate, and operate monitoring devices per manufacturer recommendations.
Keep each generator set's operating hours at or below 500 per year, calculated monthly for each consecutive 12-month period.
Operate within fuel type and sulfur content limitations—diesel only, meeting ASTM D975 S15 (<0.0015% sulfur) specification.
Maintain consumption below 583,600 gallons/year for all generators combined.
Emission limits on each set must not be exceeded as specified for NOx, CO, VOC, PM10.
Visible emissions must not exceed 10% opacity, with one 6-minute period up to 20% allowed per hour.
recordKeepingRequirements: Keep records of annual hours of operation for each generator set, calculated monthly as sum for each consecutive 12-month period.
Maintain records of annual diesel fuel consumption, calculated monthly for each consecutive 12-month period.
Keep engine info: make, model, serial number, model year, max engine power (bhp), engine displacement.
Maintain manufacturer’s operating instructions or approved owner procedures for each generator set.
Log reasons for operation for each set (date, cause, hours).
Record results of all stack/visible emission tests.
Log scheduled and unscheduled maintenance and operator training (names, dates, nature of training).
Maintain maintenance/training records for at least five years.
Document malfunctions, shutdowns, or failures causing excess emissions for more than one hour (date, time, duration, description, corrective actions, preventive measures, responsible person).
notifications: Notify EPA Region III as needed for applicable NSPS and MACT notifications.
Notify DEQ Southwest Regional Office of any malfunction causing excess emissions (>1 hour) as soon as practicable but no later than 4 business hours after discovery.
Provide written statement of malfunction (with pertinent facts, estimated duration) to DEQ within two weeks of discovery.
Notify DEQ when equipment is again in operation after malfunction correction.
Notify and provide documentation to DEQ for changes of ownership within 30 days of transfer.
